items.summaryTr: Fransa’da protestolar büyürken bütçe açığı ve ekonomik büyümeye ilişkin endişeler artıyor. Tahvil faizleri 2002’den bu yana en yüksek seviyeye çıkarken yatırımcılar, siyasi krizin piyasalar ve şirketler üzerindeki etkisini değerlendiriyor.
items.articleText: Fransa’da protestolar piyasaları sarstı: Yatırımcıların gözü üç kritik soruda Fransa’da protestolar büyürken bütçe açığı ve ekonomik büyümeye ilişkin endişeler artıyor. Tahvil faizleri 2002’den bu yana en yüksek seviyeye çıkarken yatırımcılar, siyasi krizin piyasalar ve şirketler üzerindeki etkisini değerlendiriyor. Fransa’da protestolar piyasaları sarstı! Fransa’da hükümet karşıtı protestolar, ülkenin kamu maliyesine ve ekonomik büyüme görünümüne ilişkin endişeleri artırıyor. Yeni gösteriler öncesinde yatırımcılar, siyasi belirsizliğin bütçe hedeflerini, ekonomik büyümeyi ve şirketlerin faaliyetlerini nasıl etkileyeceğini değerlendiriyor. Tahvil faizleri 2002’den bu yana en yüksek seviyeye çıkarken ülkenin kredi notu görünümü de negatifte tutuluyor. MOODY’S’TEN NEGATİF GÖRÜNÜM Fransa’nın kredi notu korundu, endişeler sürüyor Kredi derecelendirme kuruluşu Moody’s, cuma günü Fransa’nın kredi notunu Aa3 seviyesinde korudu ancak ülkenin not görünümünü negatifte tuttu. Kuruluş, Fransa’nın siyasi yapısındaki parçalanmanın yasama kurumlarının işleyişini olumsuz etkileme riskinin arttığını belirtti. Moody’s ayrıca, ülkenin bütçe açığını azaltma konusunda ilerleme kaydetmesi halinde görünümün yeniden durağana çevrilebileceğini ifade etti. HÜKÜMETİN BÜTÇE SINAVI 2027 bütçesi parlamentodan geçebilecek mi? Fransa hükümeti, bütçe açığını 2026’da gayrisafi yurt içi hasılanın yüzde 5,4’ü seviyesinden 2027’de yüzde 5’e düşürmeyi hedefliyor. Tasarruf sağlamayı amaçlayan vergi düzenlemelerinin Ulusal Meclis’te 27 Ekim’de yeniden görüşülmesi planlanıyor. Ancak muhalefet milletvekilleri hükümetin planlarına karşı çıkıyor. Bütçenin parlamentodan geçip geçmeyeceği belirsizliğini korurken hükümetin, belirli koşullarda nihai oylama olmadan yasa çıkarılmasına olanak tanıyan Anayasa’nın 49.3’üncü maddesini kullanabileceği belirtiliyor. TAHVİL FAİZLERİ 2002’DEN BU YANA ZİRVEDE Fransa’nın borçlanma maliyetleri yükseliyor Fransa’nın gösterge niteliğindeki 10 yıllık devlet tahvillerinin getirisi perşembe günü 11 baz puan yükselerek 2002’den bu yana en yüksek seviyesine çıktı. Fransız ve Alman 10 yıllık devlet tahvilleri arasındaki getiri farkı da Kasım 2011’den bu yana en geniş seviyeye ulaştı. Natixis CIB’den Alain Durré, son dönemde Fransız devlet tahvillerindeki baskının ağırlıklı olarak portföylerdeki taktiksel değişimlerden kaynaklandığını, geleneksel uzun vadeli yatırımcıların ise henüz piyasaya dönmediğini söyledi. PROTESTOLAR BÜYÜMEYİ VURABİLİR Ekonomi için büyüme tahminleri düşük ING’nin Fransa ve İsviçre Başekonomisti Charlotte de Montpellier, protestoların devam etmesi ve güvenin daha da zayıflaması halinde ekonomik büyümenin mevcut tahminlerin altında kalabileceğini belirtti. ING, Fransa ekonomisinin 2026’da yüzde 0,3, 2027’de ise yüzde 0,6 büyümesini bekliyor. De Montpellier, şiddet olaylarının tüketicileri şehir merkezlerinden uzaklaştırabileceğini, turistlerin seyahatlerini ertelemesine ve şirketlerin yatırımlarını geciktirmesine neden olabileceğini ifade etti. Geçmiş protestolar da ekonomik faaliyet üzerinde etkili olmuştu. INSEE tahminine göre Sarı Yelekliler hareketi, 2018’in son çeyreğinde Fransa’nın büyümesini 0,1 puan düşürmüş olabilir. Fransa Merkez Bankası verilerine göre 2023 baharındaki emeklilik protestoları sırasında düzenlenen grevler de ilk çeyrek büyümesini yaklaşık 0,1 puan azalttı. HANGİ SEKTÖRLER DAHA FAZLA ETKİLENECEK? Perakende, turizm ve taşımacılık öne çıkıyor Fransa’nın CAC 40 endeksi son bir ayda yüzde 4,5 geriledi. ING, protestolardan doğrudan etkilenme riski en yüksek sektörler arasında perakende, konaklama ve turizm ile taşımacılık ve lojistiği gösterdi. Mağazalar ve alışveriş merkezleri ziyaretçi sayısındaki düşüş, kapanmalar ve satış kayıplarıyla karşılaşabilir. Oteller, kafeler, restoranlar ve seyahat hizmetleri de iptal edilen faaliyetlerin daha sonra telafi edilmesinin zor olması nedeniyle risk altında bulunuyor. Süpermarket zinciri Carrefour, protestoların yanı sıra yükselen enerji maliyetlerinin tüketici güvenini olumsuz etkilediğini belirterek kâr beklentisini düşürdü ve yatırım planlarını azalttı. Şirketin hisseleri çarşamba günü yüzde 14’ten fazla geriledi. ING’nin Fransa’daki ticaret odalarının tahminlerine dayandırdığı değerlendirmesine göre salı gününe kadar 2 binden fazla işletme protestolardan doğrudan etkilenmişti. BANKALAR VE LÜKS TÜKETİM DE RİSK ALTINDA Belirsizlik şirketlerin faaliyetlerine yayılabilir Carmignac Yatırım Komitesi üyesi Kevin Thozet’ye göre siyasi belirsizliğin uzaması bankaları da etkileyebilir. Öz sermaye maliyetlerinin yükselmesi, kredi büyümesinin yavaşlaması ve kredi sorunlarının ortaya çıkması finans sektörü açısından öne çıkan riskler arasında yer alıyor. Fransa’nın lüks tüketim sektörü satışlarının büyük bölümünü yurt dışında gerçekleştiriyor. LVMH’nin 2025 gelirlerinin yüzde 8’i Fransa’dan elde edildi. Ancak protestoların turizmi ve turistlerin vergisiz alışverişlerini azaltması şirketi etkileyebilir. Thozet, Fransa’daki LVMH gelirlerinin yaklaşık yüzde 20’sinin vergisiz alışverişlerden kaynaklandığını belirtti. Fransa’da 24 Ekim için yeni gösteriler, sendikaların desteklediği ülke çapındaki grev ve protestolar içinse 5 Kasım tarihi öne çıkıyor. Yatırımcılar, eylemlerin ne kadar süreceğini ve siyasi belirsizliğin bütçe planları ile ekonomik faaliyet üzerindeki etkisini izliyor.

PROTESTOLAR BÜYÜMEYİ VURABİLİR Ekonomi için büyüme tahminleri düşük ING’nin Fransa ve İsviçre Başekonomisti Charlotte de Montpellier, protestoların devam etmesi ve güvenin daha da zayıflaması halinde ekonomik büyümenin mevcut tahminlerin altında kalabileceğini belirtti. ING, Fransa ekonomisinin 2026’da yüzde 0,3, 2027’de ise yüzde 0,6 büyümesini bekliyor. De Montpellier, şiddet olaylarının tüketicileri şehir merkezlerinden uzaklaştırabileceğini, turistlerin seyahatlerini ertelemesine ve şirketlerin yatırımlarını geciktirmesine neden olabileceğini ifade etti. Geçmiş protestolar da ekonomik faaliyet üzerinde etkili olmuştu. INSEE tahminine göre Sarı Yelekliler hareketi, 2018’in son çeyreğinde Fransa’nın büyümesini 0,1 puan düşürmüş olabilir. Fransa Merkez Bankası verilerine göre 2023 baharındaki emeklilik protestoları sırasında düzenlenen grevler de ilk çeyrek büyümesini yaklaşık 0,1 puan azalttı. HANGİ SEKTÖRLER DAHA FAZLA ETKİLENECEK? Perakende, turizm ve taşımacılık öne çıkıyor Fransa’nın CAC 40 endeksi son bir ayda yüzde 4,5 geriledi. ING, protestolardan doğrudan etkilenme riski en yüksek sektörler arasında perakende, konaklama ve turizm ile taşımacılık ve lojistiği gösterdi. Mağazalar ve alışveriş merkezleri ziyaretçi sayısındaki düşüş, kapanmalar ve satış kayıplarıyla karşılaşabilir. Oteller, kafeler, restoranlar ve seyahat hizmetleri de iptal edilen faaliyetlerin daha sonra telafi edilmesinin zor olması nedeniyle risk altında bulunuyor. Süpermarket zinciri Carrefour, protestoların yanı sıra yükselen enerji maliyetlerinin tüketici güvenini olumsuz etkilediğini belirterek kâr beklentisini düşürdü ve yatırım planlarını azalttı. Şirketin hisseleri çarşamba günü yüzde 14’ten fazla geriledi. ING’nin Fransa’daki ticaret odalarının tahminlerine dayandırdığı değerlendirmesine göre salı gününe kadar 2 binden fazla işletme protestolardan doğrudan etkilenmişti. BANKALAR VE LÜKS TÜKETİM DE RİSK ALTINDA Belirsizlik şirketlerin faaliyetlerine yayılabilir Carmignac Yatırım Komitesi üyesi Kevin Thozet’ye göre siyasi belirsizliğin uzaması bankaları da etkileyebilir. Öz sermaye maliyetlerinin yükselmesi, kredi büyümesinin yavaşlaması ve kredi sorunlarının ortaya çıkması finans sektörü açısından öne çıkan riskler arasında yer alıyor. Fransa’nın lüks tüketim sektörü satışlarının büyük bölümünü yurt dışında gerçekleştiriyor. LVMH’nin 2025 gelirlerinin yüzde 8’i Fransa’dan elde edildi. Ancak protestoların turizmi ve turistlerin vergisiz alışverişlerini azaltması şirketi etkileyebilir. Thozet, Fransa’daki LVMH gelirlerinin yaklaşık yüzde 20’sinin vergisiz alışverişlerden kaynaklandığını belirtti. Fransa’da 24 Ekim için yeni gösteriler, sendikaların desteklediği ülke çapındaki grev ve protestolar içinse 5 Kasım tarihi öne çıkıyor. Yatırımcılar, eylemlerin ne kadar süreceğini ve siyasi belirsizliğin bütçe planları ile ekonomik faaliyet üzerindeki etkisini izliyor.

items.articleText: Bill Gates 'yapay' geleceği açıkladı: İnsanlığı 20 yıllık büyük bir sarsıntı bekliyor - Bill Gates, yapay zekanın önümüzdeki 20 yılda iş hayatını ve toplumu kökten değiştirebileceği uyarısında bulundu. Gates, teknolojik dönüşümün kazananlar ve kaybedenler yaratacağını belirterek hükümetlere daha güçlü denetim ve güvenlik önlemleri çağrısı yaptı. Microsoft'un kurucu ortağı Bill Gates, yapay zeka odaklı ekonomiye geçişin önümüzdeki 20 yılda ciddi ekonomik ve toplumsal çalkantılara yol açabileceğini söyledi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Perşembe günü yayımlanan Decoder podcast'ine konuşan Gates, yapay zekanın başarıyla yönetilmesi durumunda bile bu dönüşümün kazananlar ve kaybedenler yaratacağını belirtti. Gates, “Benim en büyük endişem, kazananların ve kaybedenlerin olacağı ve büyük bir sarsıntının yaşanacağı bu 20 yıllık geçiş dönemi” dedi. Gates'e göre toplum, teknolojinin yaratabileceği olası bolluk dönemine ulaşmadan önce bu çalkantılı geçiş sürecini aşmak zorunda kalabilir. Robotlar ameliyat yapacak, ev ve gıda üretiminde görev alacak Gates, yapay zeka ve insansı robot teknolojilerindeki ilerlemelerin makinelerin bugün insanlar tarafından yapılan fiziksel işlerin önemli bir bölümünü üstlenmesini sağlayabileceğini belirtti. Bu dönüşümün ev inşaatından gıda üretimine, hatta cerrahi operasyonlara kadar uzanabileceğini ifade eden Gates, teknolojinin mal ve hizmetlere erişimdeki kıtlıkları azaltma potansiyeline de dikkat çekti. Ancak Gates, önümüzdeki 20 yıllık sürenin kesin bir tahmin olmadığını vurguladı. Geçiş döneminin uzunluğunun teknolojik ilerlemenin hızına ve yapay zekanın gelişimini yavaşlatmaya yönelik kararlara bağlı olarak değişebileceğini söyledi. Her işi makinelere bırakmak istemeyebiliriz Gates, makinelerin daha fazla işi üstlenmesine rağmen toplumların bazı faaliyetleri bilinçli olarak insanlara ayırmayı tercih edebileceğini belirtti. Çocuk bakımı, yemek hazırlama, sanat ve spor bu alanlar arasında yer aldı. Gates ayrıca yapay zekanın sağlık hizmetleri ve tarımda önemli faydalar sağlayabileceğini ifade etti. Bununla birlikte hükümetlerin ve toplumların teknolojik dönüşümün hızına yeterince hazırlıklı olmadığı uyarısında bulundu. Gates'ten hükümetlere güvenlik ve denetim çağrısı Yapay zekanın oluşturabileceği risklerin yönetilmesi için hükümetlerin daha güçlü denetim mekanizmaları kurması gerektiğini söyleyen Gates, siber saldırılar ve biyolojik tehditlere karşı teknik güvenlik önlemlerinin geliştirilmesini istedi. Yapay zeka şirketlerinin bu risklerle tek başlarına mücadele edemeyeceğini belirten Gates, hükümetlerin ve toplumun da sorumluluk üstlenmesi gerektiğini vurguladı. Gates, “İnsanlar olarak bu süreci nasıl şekillendireceğimize ilişkin seçimler yapma imkanımız var” diyerek teknolojik dönüşümün sonuçlarının alınacak kararlara bağlı olduğuna işaret etti.

items.title: Ukraine says Starlink connection 'now stable' after network limits
items.summary: The slowed Starlink connections had affected the Ukraine's military and drone operations for a week.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Ukraine says Starlink connection 'now stable' after network limits
items.summaryTr: The slowed Starlink connections had affected the Ukraine's military and drone operations for a week.
items.articleText: Ukraine says Starlink connection 'now stable' after network limits - Published Ukraine now has a "stable connection" to Starlink, its defence minister has said, after its military suffered days of restricted connectivity on the satellite internet network. Kyiv relies on the Starlink and its military-grade counterpart Starshield for piloting drones and operations within Ukraine, but last week accused US President Donald Trump of telling owner Elon Musk to place limits on it. This meant drones would lose connection when travelling at 161km/h (100mph) or more, it said. Trump denied doing so before saying Musk had "put it back". Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara said that speeds of more than 400km/h were now possible on the network, indicating that full capability had been restored. "This result is above all important for our front, for our soldiers, for the operation of drones, for logistics and for communications," he said in a statement on Saturday. Ukraine's military uses the network of 10,000 low Earth orbit satellites extensively for military operations, particularly in remote areas on the battlefield. Ukraine uses both the civilian service Starlink and the more secure Starshield, which Musk said was controlled by the US military when he suggested the Pentagon could be behind the recent issues. Russia is not authorised to use Starlink, so when Ukraine sends long-range missiles or drones deep into Russia to hit oil refineries, the network does not work. The debacle over Starlink began last week, and emerged during a broader diplomatic row between Trump and his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky over Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil infrastructure. Faced with midterm elections next month, Trump has waived some sanctions on Russia and agreed a deal to import Russian diesel for the US market - a move criticised by Ukraine and its European allies. Trump said the strikes on Russian oil refineries, which Kyiv says are crucial to stemming the main revenue source for Moscow's war effort, have pushed global prices higher. While the attacks have had an impact on global fuel prices, rises seen this year have primarily been due to the Iran war. Zelensky said that, as well as seemingly limiting Starlink capability in Ukraine, the US had also threatened to withdraw intelligence sharing if the strikes did not stop, something Trump also denied. Meanwhile, fighting on the ground continues. Russia's ministry of defence wrote on Telegram on Saturday that their air defences shot down 616 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones, striking a number of regions across the country, including Russian-annexed Crimea. Sergey Aksyonov, the region's Moscow-backed governor, said restrictions on electricity and water had been put in place because of power cuts caused by the drone strike. Meanwhile, Ukrainian authorities said they struck a missile component manufacturer, a chemical plant and an aircraft at a military airfield inside Russia in the past 24 hours. They also said that Russia carried out 88 air strikes using 309 glide bombs and 10,270 kamikaze drones on Friday. Related topics - Published15 October

items.title: U.S. Clarity Act failure gives Asia and Middle East a competitive edge, says Apex Group CEO
items.summary: Apex Group CEO Peter Hughes warned that the failure of the U.S. Clarity Act will drive digital asset businesses toward faster-moving jurisdictions in Asia and the Middle East.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: U.S. Clarity Act failure gives Asia and Middle East a competitive edge, says Apex Group CEO
items.summaryTr: Apex Group CEO Peter Hughes warned that the failure of the U.S. Clarity Act will drive digital asset businesses toward faster-moving jurisdictions in Asia and the Middle East.
items.articleText: U.S. Clarity Act failure gives Asia and Middle East a competitive edge, says Apex Group CEO Apex Group CEO Peter Hughes warned that the failure of the U.S. Clarity Act will drive digital asset businesses toward faster-moving jurisdictions in Asia and the Middle East. - The U.S. risks losing digital asset business to faster-moving jurisdictions in Asia, the Middle East and Bermuda after the Senate failed to advance the Clarity Act, Apex Group CEO Peter Hughes said. - Hughes said Europe’s crypto rules remain restrictive, while Saudi Arabia is emerging as a tokenization hub by opening its real estate market to digital assets and greater foreign investment. - Tokenized money market funds and regulated, yield-bearing stablecoins could accelerate institutional adoption by offering higher returns, collateral utility and broader access than traditional financial products, Hughes said. The U.S. risks losing digital asset business to Asia and the Middle East if it continues to delay crypto legislation or fails to implement a clear, certain regulatory framework for digital assets, said Peter Hughes, founder and CEO of Apex Group, a global financial firm. Hughes said, however, that Europe will not benefit from Washington’s setback despite having its own rules in place since July 1. “I think that the Clarity Act and the delay around that will lead to people finding other solutions elsewhere,” Hughes told CoinDesk in an interview. Hughes singled out Europe’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), describing it as slow to evolve and restrictive. “But I do think there's opportunities in Asia, which are moving quickly; the Middle East; even places like Bermuda are moving quickly around having the right regimes to really produce the product for the future, and they'll step into this gap,” he said. The U.S. Senate last month failed to pass the Clarity Act, which would have established clearer federal rules for digital assets and divided oversight between the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC). The bill fell short of the 60 votes needed in September after disputes over ethics provisions, stablecoin rewards and other regulatory concerns. Regulatory uncertainty The delay leaves uncertainty over how those products will be regulated in the world’s largest economy for companies building blockchain-based financial products.t Hughes believes faster-moving jurisdictions could attract business that might otherwise have gone to the United States. The SEC and CFTC moved soon after proposing their own set of crypto rules, in an attempt to fill the void left by lawmakers’ failure to reach consensus. Apex Group, which services more than $3.5 trillion in assets, operates across 50 jurisdictions. Earlier this month, it announced a partnership with droppRWA and Tokeny to help turn real-world assets (RWAs) into regulated blockchain-based investment products, starting in Saudi Arabia. Faisal Monai, the CEO and founder of tokenization platform droppRWA said Saudi Arabia has already made regulatory changes allowing real estate tokenization and greater foreign participation in its property market. What remains, he said, is infrastructure connecting each digital token directly to the legal record of the underlying asset. “As long as we can maintain that, then the funds will be able to convey with confidence to their investors that the asset exists, what it’s worth and who owns it,” Monai said. Hughes also suggested that U.S. banking institutions have influenced the debate around the Clarity and GENIUS acts as they seek to protect their position in the financial system. Banks have raised concerns about stablecoin rewards competing with traditional deposits, although the Senate bill faced significant objections over political ethics and regulatory safeguards. “The key thing is the scale, and that scale isn't really in these areas,” he said. Beyond Clarity Beyond the regulatory debate, Hughes sees tokenized money market funds as one of the biggest drivers of institutional adoption. These funds invest in traditional short-term debt but issue blockchain-based tokens representing investors’ holdings. Hughes argued that they could compete with bank savings accounts by passing more of the investment returns directly to customers. Hughes cited a comparison of 5% returns from a tokenized money market fund against 3% from a bank savings account. He said the difference in returns could become an important reason for investors to choose tokenized money market funds over traditional bank savings accounts as adoption grows. Another advantage, according to Hughes, is that tokenized funds can be used as collateral, allowing institutions to borrow against their holdings rather than leaving the money tied up in traditional investment accounts. He said major banks are already examining that use. Hughes expects regulated, yield-bearing stablecoins to become an important tool for corporate treasuries, provided issuers meet requirements including reserve transparency. “Whether that happens in one, three, or five years, it's hard to judge,” the Bermuda-based financial firm’s CEO added. Hughes said he expects tokenization to reach a wider range of investors, including retirement accounts and retail customers, as regulators become more comfortable with the technology. Smaller investment amounts, faster product creation and broader distribution could help bring traditional financial products to people who previously had limited access, he said. Monai sees a similar opportunity in Saudi Arabia, predicting that tokenization could eventually become a mainstream way for foreign investors to put capital into the country without having to establish local presence. “I foresee that tokenization will be the mainstream for capital moving into Saudi Arabia,” Monai said. Diversified RWA stablecoins sustain 5-7% yield from real credit as crypto funding compresses to ~4%. GENIUS pushes yield off-chain; TAM grows to $4B in 3 years. Earlier this month, it announced a partnership with droppRWA and Tokeny to help turn real-world assets (RWAs) into regulated blockchain-based investment products, starting in Saudi Arabia. Faisal Monai, the CEO and founder of tokenization platform droppRWA said Saudi Arabia has already made regulatory changes allowing real estate tokenization and greater foreign participation in its property market. What remains, he said, is infrastructure connecting each digital token directly to the legal record of the underlying asset. “As long as we can maintain that, then the funds will be able to convey with confidence to their investors that the asset exists, what it’s worth and who owns it,” Monai said. Hughes also suggested that U.S. banking institutions have influenced the debate around the Clarity and GENIUS acts as they seek to protect their position in the financial system. Banks have raised concerns about stablecoin rewards competing with traditional deposits, although the Senate bill faced significant objections over political ethics and regulatory safeguards. “The key thing is the scale, and that scale isn't really in these areas,” he said. Beyond Clarity Beyond the regulatory debate, Hughes sees tokenized money market funds as one of the biggest drivers of institutional adoption. These funds invest in traditional short-term debt but issue blockchain-based tokens representing investors’ holdings. Hughes argued that they could compete with bank savings accounts by passing more of the investment returns directly to customers. Hughes cited a comparison of 5% returns from a tokenized money market fund against 3% from a bank savings account. He said the difference in returns could become an important reason for investors to choose tokenized money market funds over traditional bank savings accounts as adoption grows. Another advantage, according to Hughes, is that tokenized funds can be used as collateral, allowing institutions to borrow against their holdings rather than leaving the money tied up in traditional investment accounts. He said major banks are already examining that use. Hughes expects regulated, yield-bearing stablecoins to become an important tool for corporate treasuries, provided issuers meet requirements including reserve transparency. “Whether that happens in one, three, or five years, it's hard to judge,” the Bermuda-based financial firm’s CEO added. Hughes said he expects tokenization to reach a wider range of investors, including retirement accounts and retail customers, as regulators become more comfortable with the technology. Smaller investment amounts, faster product creation and broader distribution could help bring traditional financial products to people who previously had limited access, he said. Monai sees a similar opportunity in Saudi Arabia, predicting that tokenization could eventually become a mainstream way for foreign investors to put capital into the country without having to establish local presence. “I foresee that tokenization will be the mainstream for capital moving into Saudi Arabia,” Monai said. Diversified RWA stablecoins sustain 5-7% yield from real credit as crypto funding compresses to ~4%. GENIUS pushes yield off-chain; TAM grows to $4B in 3 years. items.summaryTr: Charlotte Riley says more families are reaching out for help for a variety of reasons.
items.articleText: Rising demand from families needing Christmas help - Published The number of families asking for help to afford Christmas presents is rising, according to the organiser of a charitable cause. For the past two years Charlotte Riley has collected and distributed donated gifts voluntarily as part of Christmas Kindness Appeal Jersey which she organises through Facebook. The gifts are given to families for children aged up to 18. Riley said: "What we are seeing is that each year we're getting more and more numbers coming through." She said the donated gifts helped to "take the pressure off" families in need of support. Riley said when she first started the appeal in 2024 she "didn't expect the response from the community". She said: "I knew there were people in need. "I didn't quite know how many people that would be." She said the reasons people might reach out to the appeal included unemployment, ill health and the general high cost of living. Along with more demand, Riley said there were also increasing numbers of people offering to help. "It wouldn't be done without those other people helping," she said. "We have people doing deliveries, we have people doing pickups... we have people that have accessed this and got gifts in previous years that are now saying 'I want to give back' so they will go and do collections for us as well." Riley said there was a three-week window for donations which can include clothes, food and essentials as well as gifts. Donations can be made before 14 November. "People are very complimentary and very thankful," Riley said. She said she wanted parents to feel part of the process so they were also given wrapping paper and labels. "It's the small simple things as well that make that big difference," she said. Follow BBC Jersey on X, external, Facebook, external and Instagram, external. items.summaryTr: The campaign, run by Little Stars, is running from today until 4 December.
items.articleText: Charity expects demand for Christmas present campaign - Published A Shropshire charity has said it expects demand to be high this year for its campaign which provides Christmas presents to struggling families. Little Stars, which gives away free essentials to families in need, has launched Santa's Little Stars, which runs from Saturday 24 October to Friday 4 December. The public is asked to donate new, unwrapped toys and gifts to donation points in Shrewsbury's Darwin shopping centre. Donations are wrapped and given to children from birth to age 17, as well as pregnant women who are referred to the charity. Little Stars said 2025 was its biggest campaign year to date, and it expected demand to continue to be high due to many families continuing to face financial pressures. The charity launched Santa's Little Stars in 2020 and has given out more than 8,000 presents in that time, supporting more than 2,100 children. It added that donations could be taken to collection points outside the Collective, The Entertainer, Home Bargains and Clarks Shoes. items.titleTr: Woman, 65, becomes second patient to die of Ebola in Kenya
items.summaryTr: She was a close family member of the first victim, a man who had travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo.
items.articleText: Woman, 65, becomes second patient to die of Ebola in Kenya - Published Kenya has recorded its second death from Ebola as it handles its first ever outbreak of the disease. A woman, aged 65, who was a close family member of the first victim, a man who had travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo, died after being placed in quarantine, the health ministry said. Seven other Ebola patients were receiving treatment at two isolation facilities, it added. All the cases were within "one cluster, with no evidence of community spread", the ministry said. More than 4,000 people have died in Africa since Ebola was confirmed in DR Congo in May, making it the second most deadly outbreak of the disease. Kenya's latest victim had been under quarantine when she developed symptoms on 13 October, the health ministry said. The first death, on 5 October, was that of a man who fell ill in September and was treated in several hospitals in DR Congo before arriving in the Kenyan capital, Nairobi, where he died a few days later. Those still being treated are three other relatives of the first victim, three health workers and a hospital cleaner. The US has warned its citizens against travelling to Kenya, while neighbouring countries such as Uganda, Ethiopia and Somalia are also on alert. Ebola is a rare but deadly disease, external caused by a virus. As the disease progresses, vomiting and diarrhoea develop and it can lead to organ failure. Some, but not all, patients develop internal and external bleeding. The disease spreads from one person to another by contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit. The Bundibugyo species of Ebola is relatively rare, with no approved vaccine or treatment - though trials are under way. With more than 9,500 cases in DR Congo, Kenya faces a steady risk of new cases arriving across borders, according to the International Rescue Committee, which has been working alongside both governments to contain the spread. Kenya has introduced enhanced screening for travellers arriving from DR Congo and nine other countries it considers to be at high risk: Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi, Angola, Zambia, Ethiopia, South Sudan and the Central African Republic. Travellers arriving from those countries are required to complete a digital surveillance form before boarding their flights and present a QR code to port health officials on arrival. Kenya also ordered enhanced public health screening of aircraft arriving from those countries, as authorities seek to prevent further imported cases. Within the country, the government has been sharing public messages to create awareness about Ebola, including encouraging people to promptly report any suspected cases and seek care at a hospital. - Is Ebola under control in Kenya after nine cases confirmed? - Published3 days ago - Woman with Ebola in Nigeria confirmed as wife of Swiss diplomat - Published1 day ago Nigeria's health minister said its sole confirmed case of Ebola appeared to be genetically related to a strain identified earlier in Kenya. Prof Ali Pate said there was no evidence so far that the Kenyan patient had travelled to Nigeria, but that further testing was under way. Health officials have been investigating whether Nigeria's first case crossed paths with Kenya's first patient. Both are believed to have travelled through Uganda's Entebbe airport earlier this month. Uganda's health ministry announced on Friday that people who had travelled to DR Congo would no longer be able to transit via Uganda as part of its prevention measures. items.summary: Two subscriptions on Thursday nearly quadrupled the fund’s tokens on the network. The receiving wallet shares its authorized signers with the issuer.

items.titleTr: Franklin Templeton adds $150 million in fund shares to XRP Ledger, all in one wallet
items.summaryTr: Two subscriptions on Thursday nearly quadrupled the fund’s tokens on the network. The receiving wallet shares its authorized signers with the issuer.
items.articleText: Franklin Templeton adds $150 million in fund shares to XRP Ledger, all in one wallet Two subscriptions on Thursday nearly quadrupled the fund’s tokens on the network. The receiving wallet shares its authorized signers with the issuer. - Franklin Templeton added about $150 million in shares of its tokenized money market fund to the XRP Ledger, bringing the network’s total to nearly 193 million shares worth about $200 million. - All sgBENJI shares on the XRP Ledger remain in a single wallet that shares transaction signers with Franklin’s issuing account, though it is unclear whether the wallet represents one investor or multiple clients. - The fund invests in short-term dollar debt and money-market instruments, and its XRP Ledger holdings can be approved, frozen or recovered by Franklin. Franklin Templeton added $150 million worth of shares in its tokenized money market fund to the XRP Ledger earlier Friday, with every new share went to one wallet which now holds the fund’s entire token balance on the network. That wallet and Franklin’s issuing account authorize the identical eight signing addresses. Any two can jointly approve a transaction, according to CoinDesk’s review of ledger records. The wallet holds nearly 193 million sgBENJI shares, up from about 48 million before Thursday. At the $1.039 share price recorded in the transactions, that is worth about $200 million. RWA.xyz ranks Franklin second in its XRP Ledger table of tokenized asset platforms, behind Ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin at about $930 million and ahead of Ondo at $185 million. Each token represents a share of the Singapore-domiciled Franklin OnChain U.S. Dollar Short-Term Money Market Fund. It invests in short-term dollar debt and money-market instruments, including government paper, commercial paper and bank deposits. Returns accumulate in the share price. On Wednesday, Franklin’s issuing account wrote two subscription receipts onto the ledger. Each recorded a $75 million cash subscription and carried its own reference code. Two batches of just over 72,184,793 shares followed at 02:58 and 04:13 UTC Thursday, each carrying a matching receipt code and a $1.039 share price. The receipts leave the investors, funding source and any connection to existing holdings on Stellar, the other blockchain the fund uses, undisclosed. RWA.xyz lists Franklin’s XRP Ledger position at about $193 million, matching the share count at a dollar each. Thursday’s recorded share price puts its value nearly $8 million higher. Why one wallet Brokers and custodians routinely hold shares for many clients in one account, tracking individual ownership separately. Franklin’s fund documents describe a register combining blockchain entries with records held outside the network, including information “which links the wallet addresses of the entries on the distributed ledger to their real-world identities.” Whether this particular wallet represents one investor or several remains unclear. CoinDesk asked Franklin whether it is an omnibus account, how many investors funded the subscriptions and whether they or their custodians will receive tokens in separate addresses. The firm had not responded as of Asia morning hours on Saturday. Franklin and DBS announced the fund’s Singapore-authorized structure in November 2025 with a $20 minimum investment. Initially available to wealth and accredited clients, retail access was expected in early 2026. Their September 2025 agreement with Ripple outlined plans for eligible DBS Digital Exchange clients to switch between sgBENJI and RLUSD. DBS also said it would explore lending against the fund tokens. Holding sgBENJI directly on XRPL requires Franklin’s approval. Its settings also allow the issuer to freeze balances and recover tokens. Thursday’s transactions nearly quadrupled the number of sgBENJI shares on the XRP Ledger. The number of wallets holding any of them stayed at one. GENIUS pushes yield off-chain; TAM grows to $4B in 3 years. Why it matters: Diversified RWA stablecoins sustain 5-7% yield from real credit as crypto funding compresses to ~4%. items.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Louisiana Man and His Companies to Pay Over $9 Million in Forex Fraud
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Louisiana Man and His Companies to Pay Over $9 Million in Forex Fraud
items.articleText: Release Number 9313-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Louisiana Man and His Companies to Pay Over $9 Million in Forex Fraud October 21, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Louisiana entered a default judgment against defendants Michael B. DePetrillo, Meteor LLC, and NOLA FX Capital Management LLC for their participation in a fraudulent retail forex scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented that participant funds would be used to trade retail forex, made material misrepresentations and omissions regarding the profitability of forex trading with them, and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying DePetrillo’s personal expenses, and trading in DePetrillo’s personal account. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,211,492 civil monetary penalty. The order also permanently enjoins the defendants from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposes permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2024 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9003-24] On Feb. 18, 2025, in a related criminal case, DePetrillo pleaded guilty to violating the Commodity Exchange Act in connection with the same conduct in the CFTC’s complaint. On July 23, 2025, the court sentenced him to nine years in prison and ordered him to pay $6,748,412 in restitution. The CFTC appreciates the assistance of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Louisiana and the FBI New Orleans Division. -CFTC-

items.title: CFTC Secures Federal Court Orders Requiring Former Long Island Resident and His Firm to Pay Over $288 Million for Operating a Commodity Pool Ponzi Scheme
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC Secures Federal Court Orders Requiring Former Long Island Resident and His Firm to Pay Over $288 Million for Operating a Commodity Pool Ponzi Scheme
items.articleText: Release Number 9311-26 CFTC Secures Federal Court Orders Requiring Former Long Island Resident and His Firm to Pay Over $288 Million for Operating a Commodity Pool Ponzi Scheme October 19, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York entered orders granting the CFTC’s motions for summary judgment, injunctive relief, and a civil monetary penalty against Eddy Alexandre of Valley Stream, New York, and his company, EminiFX Inc., which operated in Valley Stream and Manhattan, New York. The orders require the defendants to pay $228,576,962 in restitution to the defrauded investors, to disgorge $15,049,500 in unlawful gains of (offset by any amounts paid in restitution), and to pay a $45,148,500 penalty. The orders stem from the CFTC’s May 12, 2022, complaint in this matter. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8527-22.] As described in the court’s summary judgment order, the defendants held themselves out as an investment club providing investors with an affordable solution that offered easy access to cryptocurrency and Forex trading using the latest technology available. Over the course of EminiFX’s eight months in operation, tens of thousands of investors sent contributions exceeding $262 million. According to the order, the defendants reported “astonishing” returns on investment of 5% to 9.99% per week. In reality, EminiFX experienced net losses exceeding $49 million. At least $15 million of those losses resulted from Alexandre’s misappropriation of investor funds for his own use. As noted by the court, “Simply put, EminiFX was a Ponzi scheme, and investors’ decisions to give their money to [d]efendants was predicated entirely on fraudulent misrepresentations.” During the CFTC’s lawsuit, the court-appointed receiver recovered millions of dollars in investor funds and other assets held by the defendants and is distributing those funds to the defrauded investors. As of July 2026, over $98 million has been returned to more than 28,000 investors. The CFTC cautions, however, that orders requiring repayment of funds to victims may not always result in the recovery of lost money because the wrongdoers may not have sufficient funds or assets. Alexandre is serving a nine-year prison sentence based on a parallel action for related conduct brought by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York. -CFTC-

items.title: CFTC Seeks Public Comment on Notice of Proposed Rulemaking Concerning the Inclusion of Certain Event Contracts in the Definition of Swap
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC Seeks Public Comment on Notice of Proposed Rulemaking Concerning the Inclusion of Certain Event Contracts in the Definition of Swap
items.articleText: Release Number 9310-26 CFTC Seeks Public Comment on Notice of Proposed Rulemaking Concerning the Inclusion of Certain Event Contracts in the Definition of Swap October 09, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today published a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking that proposes providing additional market clarity by expressly further defining the term “swap” to include event contracts, including those based on sports, politics, cultural, and weather-related events. The proposal notes these contracts are financial instruments that are commonly known to the trade as swaps and proposes to resolve any ambiguity regarding these contracts. “Americans use event contracts to hedge risks, speculate, and provide the public with information about the outcome of future events,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “These products are commodity derivatives squarely within the CFTC’s regulatory remit under the Commodity Exchange Act and are within the agency’s exclusive jurisdiction.” Comments to the NPRM must be submitted in writing via Regulations.gov and received within 30 days of the NPRM’s publication in the Federal Register. -CFTC-

items.title: CFTC Issues Interim Final Rule Excluding Certain Activity from the Definition of Swap
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC Issues Interim Final Rule Excluding Certain Activity from the Definition of Swap
items.articleText: Release Number 9309-26 CFTC Issues Interim Final Rule Excluding Certain Activity from the Definition of Swap October 09, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today published an Interim Final Rule that codifies the CFTC’s longstanding position that casino-style gambling products, including wagers placed on sportsbooks and casino games, are excluded from the “swap” definition. “Casino-style gambling products are not derivatives,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Just as the CFTC has done with respect to other products historically regulated by the states, the Commission today provides clarity regarding the limits of its regulatory remit by codifying the exclusion of casino-style gambling products from the ‘swap’ definition.” The IFR will be effective immediately upon publication in the Federal Register and written comments must be received via Regulations.gov within 30 days of the IFR’s publication in the Federal Register. -CFTC-
